utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, people were talking about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You talked about this officer who you described when prompted by Mr. Vasic. He came along, he gave that order for men to be separated off, some to the left and some to the right, you said he was about 50 years old. What I want to know is, do you think you would be able to recognise this man if you saw him again? Is his face lodged in your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I would be able to identify that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can we have Exhibit 338 shown, please? The ERN number is -- I'm sorry, 0036-6995. This is Exhibit 338. Not the photograph. 0036-6995. And this is 6973, so what I want is 6995. There we go. Sir, have a look, please. Look at this photograph closely. Is this an environment that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I saw this at the time, but I recognise this to be the nuclear shelter in the basement of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In this photograph you see a man wearing a uniform, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Might that perhaps be the officer you saw at the Vukovar Hospital on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: But you can't rule out the possibility, can you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're quite right. I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Aside from this officer, the officer you have mentioned, the officer who ordered for the men to be separated off in the way that you described, did you see any other officers arriving at the Vukovar Hospital with this one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember about inside the hospital, several officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You have your statement in front of you; you gave this statement to the centre for gathering information and processing data regarding the Homeland War. The date is the 6th of July, 1994. Can you find that statement for us, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of my learned friends, the ERN number is 2746, being the last four digits.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the first four digits.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, have you got that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I have the date, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The 6th of July, 1994.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Have you got that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please read paragraph 2, which reads: "On the 20th of November in the morning."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 20th of November in the morning at around 8.00 a group of JNA officers arrived and ordered for the women, children and wounded who could still move about to leave the hospital compound. After that we" --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, thank you. I'm not interested in the rest of this. Is this your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see a reference there to a group of officers who arrived in the hospital and ordered -- and so on and so forth. So not just one, a group of them in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If back in 1994 I said there were several, that should be more accurate than what I'm saying now. This was 12 years ago. My memory was a lot more vivid.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you then allow for the possibility that the officer you have mentioned who was conducting the frisking and those other ones was perhaps not the only officer checking the injuries of those inside the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do allow for that possibility, yes. Especially in view of the fact that they might have been in other rooms, rooms that I was not in myself. I was in the hospital hall. I didn't go anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You talked about a list. And then names were called out based on that list of hospital patients?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many names exactly were called out from this list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About five or six names, as far as I remember. Up to 10, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All the names were called out and at this point one of those officers told you to leave and go outside. How much time elapsed between the order and the time you eventually left the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of minutes. Two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: From the moment you left the hospital building to the moment the officer arrived that you identified as Veselin Sljivancanin, how much time elapsed between these two things happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five to 10 minutes, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You referred in your testimony to a number of names of people who were on the bus with you and who went to Ovcara with you. What I want to know is: Were any of the people you mentioned standing there with you before the frisking began? Do you remember anyone? Could you name anyone who was standing there with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember anyone who was there during the frisking. But there are two lines of people lined up against the wall, and your angle of vision does not really cover a lot of your surroundings. You see the two men standing right next to you on either side but not much else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: We know about that officer who you described the way you did. You identified this officer as Veselin Sljivancanin. Can you tell me exactly what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a uniform, a Tito cap, and military boots.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of uniform? Was this the traditional olive-drab uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. I think some components of the uniform were camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Where was his rank displayed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you to define the person's rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear you properly. Can you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Where did he have his rank displayed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing his rank displayed on the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say Sljivancanin stayed there for about 15 minutes. And then you left for the buses and you didn't see Sljivancanin after that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see him at the barracks when the buses arrived, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him again, full stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't see him at the barracks, and you didn't see him at Ovcara. We agree on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We definitely do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we have Exhibit 256 shown, photograph number 13. The ERN is 0053-1243.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the buildings in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a bird's eye view of the Vukovar barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher could help you and hand you a pen, which you can use to make markings on the screen. Can you please mark where the buses were at the time you were brought into the barracks? Try to mark this semi-circle, the disposition of the buses that were parked there. Can you mark that, please? After that I would like to ask you to use a special mark for your own bus.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine. It was like this. This is how the buses arrived, like this. [Marks]. And I think there was one bus right here. [Marks]. The next one was parked just in front of it. This was the third bus. [Marks]. The fourth bus. [Marks]. And the fifth bus. [Marks]. This was the arrangement, the spacial arrangement, roughly speaking. My own bus was right here. I am circling my own bus and I'm marking it with a number 1. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. Were you seated on the left-hand side of the bus or on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right-hand side. The seats at the rear, at the rear door. The two extra seats, auxiliary seats.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived it was quiet at first, if I understand you correctly, and then some paramilitaries arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a lot of commotion from the moment we got there. There was a turmoil. Threats were being made. A lot of people milling about, wearing all sorts of different uniforms, peering through the bus windows, yelling at us, brandishing knives. It was in this area that they smashed some sort of civil protection closet and extracted from it some spades and axes. They splintered some sort of a log that was there. All they kept were handles. They said they would go and sharpen their knives, and then we heard the sound of knives being sharpened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. We heard that yesterday. Let me ask you this: On your way out of the hospital, or at least this is what you indicated in your statement to the OTP, you said names were called out by this officer holding a list. He called out the names of some people, including the three Dosen brothers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we're back at hospital now, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: My apologies. I seem to have got my chronology in a twist, so I think I skipped that previously. The three Dosen brothers were taken away and you never saw them again; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek that this marked photograph be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 529, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]. We don't need the photograph now. The usher is now free to go back to his seat. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The buses at Ovcara, how were those emptied? One by one and then on to the hangar, or all at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One by one, and people got off the bus on an individual basis. One by one. Not en masse, as it were. As soon as someone got off the bus this person would immediately be beaten, and the buses were parked in such a way to make it possible for people to go straight into the gauntlet.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see what was happening to the buses which had just been emptied, were they moved elsewhere or did they just leave them right there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Based on all of your statements I noticed that you draw a distinction between the regular JNA, the so-called JNA on the one hand, and Chetniks on the other. Would that seem to be a fair assessment, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This gauntlet that was set up, did that comprise any JNA men, members of the regular JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. Most of the men standing there -- or, rather, some of the men standing there were wearing JNA uniforms but they were slightly older and they were more unkempt than regular JNA recruits. They struck me as TO members who were wearing the same kind of uniform, generally speaking. There were some people in that gauntlet wearing no uniforms, no proper uniforms at all, but who were displaying Chetnik insignia, cockades, long beards, long hair, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You are a local from Vukovar. Did you notice any local faces there in that gauntlet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the far end there were several of those, yes. I recognised one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Once you were inside the hangar what time was it, roughly speaking? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really be very specific at all, but you could have a proper time-line if you go from dusk backwards, or the other way around, but it's very difficult for me to say exactly what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You remember there being a desk inside the hangar and someone seated at that desk obviously trying to draw up a list of people inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember a rope inside the hangar used to separate the groups of people inside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What sort of rope are you talking about separating groups of people inside?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let me clarify this. We have heard evidence here that there was a rope inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what a rope is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This rope was strung the whole breadth of the hangar in order to separate the various groups of people inside, to keep them apart?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that particular detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the officer you described who had a whistle, and you told us why you thought he was a security officer, and that was because the person who gave him the list told you he was a security officer, were there other people there who you think were officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along with him there were two others, or three, who I thought were officers. JNA officers, that is. I recognised them by their uniforms, ranks, Tito caps, and because they were older than the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were these junior or senior officers? Can you tell us something about their age, their uniforms, their ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-030 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wore olive-drab uniforms, they had ranks on their shoulders, they wore Tito caps. They were aged around 40 or 45 and up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move into private session now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Might being advisable to do it tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Yes. So we shall do it tomorrow morning. Then unfortunately, Witness, we can't finish today, so you will have to come back tomorrow morning, but it hopefully will be very short. So we will resume and gather tomorrow at 9.00 because we have a morning session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
